south-africa/tradouw-highlands.text: A ward in the Klein Karoo area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/tulbagh.text: A district in the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/tygerberg.text: A district in the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape, with Durbanville and Philadelphia inside.

south-africa/upper-hemel-en-aarde-valley.text: A ward in the Walker Bay area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/upper-langkloof.text: A ward in the Klein Karoo area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/vinkrivier.text: A ward in the Robertson district of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/voor-paardeberg.text: A ward in the Paarl area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/vredendal.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/walker-bay.text: A district on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape, with Bot River, Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge, Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Sunday's Glen and Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley inside.

south-africa/wellington.text: A ward in the Paarl area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/western-cape.text: A geographical unit within the Wine of Origin system, matching the Western Cape province and taking in most of South Africa's vineyards. It holds the Coastal Region, Breede River Valley, Cape South Coast, Klein Karoo and Olifants River.

argentina.text: The world's sixth-largest wine producer in 2025, with vine cuttings first brought to Santiago del Estero in 1557. Malbec is the most planted grape at 24%, followed by Cereza and Bonarda. Its provinces include San Juan, Mendoza and Río Negro.

argentina/25-de-mayo.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. The planting figures list only Isabella.

argentina/agrelo.text: A wine area in Luján de Cuyo, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/albardon.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Plantings are led by Cereza (37%), Superior Seedless (25%) and Cardinal (8%).

argentina/alto-agrelo.text: A wine area in Luján de Cuyo, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/alto-valle-de-rio-negro.text: A wine area in Río Negro, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces.

argentina/angaco.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Plantings are led by Cereza (46%), Torrontés Sanjuanino (13%) and Pedro Giménez (5%).

argentina/avellaneda.text: A wine area in Río Negro, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Malbec leads plantings at 32%, followed by Merlot (12%) and Pinot Noir (8%).

argentina/barrancas.text: A wine area in Maipú, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/barreal.text: A wine area in Calingasta, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/cachi.text: A wine area in Salta, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Malbec dominates plantings at 77%, followed by Merlot (5%) and Pinot Noir (4%).

argentina/cafayate.text: A wine area in Salta, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Malbec leads plantings at 48%, followed by Torrontés Riojano (20%) and Cabernet Sauvignon (15%).

argentina/calingasta.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces, with Barreal, Hilario, Sorocayense and Tamberías inside. Malbec dominates plantings at 64%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (17%) and Syrah (3%).

argentina/canota.text: A wine area in Las Heras, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/caucete.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces, with Pozo de los Algarrobos inside. Plantings are led by Cereza (29%), Syrah (8%) and Malbec (7%).

argentina/chimbas.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Cereza dominates plantings at 56%, followed by Muscat of Alexandria (6%) and Syrah (6%).

argentina/chubut.text: A province in Argentine wine country, with El Hoyo and Trevelin as the wine areas inside it.

argentina/confluencia.text: A wine area in Neuquén, Argentina. Malbec leads plantings at 40%, followed by Pinot Noir (16%) and Chardonnay (9%).

argentina/distrito-medrano.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/el-paraiso.text: A wine area in Maipú, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/general-alvear.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Plantings are led by Cereza (21%), Criolla Grande (16%) and Bonarda (12%).

argentina/general-conesa.text: A wine area in Río Negro, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces.

argentina/general-roca.text: A wine area in Río Negro, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Malbec leads plantings at 23%, followed by Merlot (15%) and Pinot Noir (10%).

argentina/godoy-cruz.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. The planting figures list only Malbec.

argentina/guaymallen.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Malbec leads plantings at 25%, followed by Syrah (11%) and Bonarda (10%).

argentina/hilario.text: A wine area in Calingasta, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/iglesia.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Plantings are led by Malbec (40%) and Torrontés Sanjuanino (40%).

argentina/junin.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Malbec leads plantings at 18%, followed by Criolla Grande (15%) and Cereza (14%).

argentina/la-cienaga.text: A wine area in Zonda, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/la-paz.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Plantings are led by Cereza (18%), Cabernet Sauvignon (15%) and Bonarda (14%).

argentina/las-compuertas.text: A wine area in Luján de Cuyo, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/las-heras.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with Canota inside. Plantings are led by Cereza (15%), Bonarda (13%) and Pedro Giménez (13%).

argentina/lavalle.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Plantings are led by Bonarda (17%), Cereza (13%) and Syrah (12%).

argentina/lujan-de-cuyo.text: A wine area that is both an IG and a DOC in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with Agrelo, Alto Agrelo, Las Compuertas and Vistalba inside. Malbec dominates plantings at 58%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (13%) and Bonarda (4%).

argentina/lunlunta.text: A wine area in Maipú, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/maipu.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with Barrancas, El Paraíso, Lunlunta and Russel inside. Malbec leads plantings at 37%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (12%) and Bonarda (8%).

argentina/mendoza.text: Argentina's most important wine region, making nearly two-thirds of the country's wine. Vineyards sit high in the eastern foothills of the Andes, and Malbec is the leading grape.

argentina/molinos.text: A wine area in Salta, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Malbec dominates plantings at 68%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (14%) and Sauvignon Blanc (4%).

argentina/neuquen.text: An Argentine wine area with two places inside it, Añelo and Confluencia.

argentina/pichimahuida.text: A wine area in Río Negro, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Plantings are led by Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains (20%), Malbec (16%) and Pedro Giménez (12%).

argentina/pocito.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Cereza leads its wine-grape plantings, then Syrah.

argentina/pozo-de-los-algarrobos.text: A wine area in Caucete, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/rawson.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Cereza dominates plantings at 52%, followed by Pedro Giménez (10%) and Syrah (7%).

argentina/reduccion.text: A wine area in Rivadavia, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/rio-negro.text: A wine-producing province of Argentina, with Alto Valle de Río Negro, Avellaneda, General Conesa, General Roca and Pichimahuida inside. In El Cuy, Malbec (38%) and Merlot (32%) lead the plantings.

argentina/rivadavia.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with Reducción inside. Malbec leads plantings at 17%, followed by Criolla Grande (15%) and Bonarda (12%).

argentina/russel.text: A wine area in Maipú, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/san-carlos.text: A group of wine areas in Salta, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces, with Valle de Pucará inside. Plantings are led by Torrontés Riojano (49%), Malbec (30%) and Cabernet Sauvignon (7%).

argentina/san-carlos-in-valle-de-uco.text: A wine area in Mendoza, with Cordón el Cepillo, La Consulta, Pampa el Cepillo and Paraje Altamira inside. Malbec dominates the plantings at 64%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon and Tempranillo.

argentina/san-juan.text: An Argentine province and one of its most important wine regions, containing 25 de Mayo, Albardón, Calingasta, Iglesia, Pocito, Zonda and others. In Calingasta and Iglesia, the figures show Malbec at 64% and Cabernet Sauvignon at 17%.

argentina/san-martin.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Plantings are led by Criolla Grande and Cereza (17% each), then Bonarda (14%).

argentina/san-rafael.text: A wine area that is both an IG and a DOC in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Malbec leads plantings at 18%, followed by Bonarda (13%) and Cabernet Sauvignon (9%).

argentina/santa-lucia.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces. Cereza dominates plantings at 54%, followed by Bonarda (7%) and Malbec (5%).

argentina/santa-rosa.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province. Plantings are led by Cereza (16%), Bonarda (15%) and Criolla Grande (12%).

argentina/sarmiento.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces, with Valle del Pedernal inside. Plantings are led by Cereza (27%), Malbec (14%) and Pedro Giménez (9%).

argentina/sorocayense.text: A wine area in Calingasta, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/tamberias.text: A wine area in Calingasta, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/tunuyan.text: A wine area in Valle de Uco, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with Los Chacayes, San Pablo and Vista Flores inside. Malbec dominates plantings at 55%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (12%) and Chardonnay (5%).

argentina/tupungato.text: A wine area in Valle de Uco, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with El Peral inside. Malbec leads plantings at 47%, followed by Chardonnay (11%) and Cabernet Sauvignon (9%).

argentina/valle-de-pucara.text: A wine area in San Carlos, in Salta, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces.

argentina/valle-de-uco.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with San Carlos, Tupungato and Tunuyán inside. Malbec dominates plantings at 55%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (10%) and Chardonnay (7%).

argentina/valle-de-zonda.text: A wine area in Zonda, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/valle-del-pedernal.text: A wine area in Sarmiento, in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/valle-del-tulum.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces.

argentina/vistalba.text: A wine area in Luján de Cuyo, in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province.

argentina/zonda.text: A wine area in San Juan, one of Argentina's most important wine provinces, with the IGs La Ciénaga-Zonda and Valle de Zonda inside. Malbec leads plantings at 29%, followed by Muscat of Alexandria (14%) and Superior Seedless (10%).

argentina/salta.text: A wine-producing province of Argentina, with Cachi, Cafayate, Molinos and San Carlos inside. Argentina's most important wine regions are in Mendoza, San Juan and La Rioja, and Salta is among the other wine-producing provinces.
